subject: Deployment mode & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment mode & pricing follow-up

Hi Elaine — great to meet today. Quick recap from our call and next steps on deployment mode and cost options so we can size things properly: 

1) Acme needs/priorities (as I understood them):
- In-store real-time recommendations with P50 latency target <200ms (per-request).
- High-volume batch scoring for nightly analytics (throughput over latency).
- Data residency requirement for EU customer subset and some PII controls.

2) Deployment mode fit (high-level):
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, no infra ops, pay-as-you-go (per-token). Great for POCs and parts of the workflow that don't require dedicated SLAs or strict network isolation.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Good if you need sustained QPS and want a committed monthly price. Supports canary rollouts and autoscaling policies.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation and customer-controlled KMS/HSM. Recommended for regulated workloads or when Acme requires on-prem instances for certain datasets.

3) Immediate ask from us to size cost models:
- Average request QPS (peak and baseline) for the in-store use case.
- Average prompt + response token estimate per request (or example payload).
- Expected monthly request volume and batch scoring throughput (TPH).
- Any hard procurement or contract timing constraints (PO lead time, security review).

Attached is a starter pricing model (Acme_MA_Pricing_Model.xlsx) with two baseline scenarios we can iterate on.

Next step: if you can confirm the QPS and token estimates I’ll share a short deck and a side-by-side cost calc (hosted per-token vs committed dedicated pool) and loop in Marissa to run a short dedicated throughput demo.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Acme_MA_Pricing_Model.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet)

From: Elaine Park <elaine@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & pricing follow-up

Thanks Aditya — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side before we jump to a demo: 

- For the in-store recommender: baseline 150 QPS across 200 stores, peak 600 QPS during promos. Typical request size ~ 40 input tokens + 60 output tokens (100 tokens total) for recommendations.
- Batch scoring: we run 5M user-item evaluations nightly (can be parallelized).
- Residency: only EU customer data must remain in EU; US data can be hosted elsewhere.

Primary question from procurement: we want a high-level monthly cost comparison for two options:
A) Hosted API (pay-as-you-go per-token) — estimate for 10M requests/month at the token counts above.
B) Dedicated capacity (committed) — what committed GPU pool would you recommend and an estimated monthly committed cost plus estimated effective per-request cost.

Also curious about burst handling: if we commit to a dedicated pool, can we burst to hosted for spikes? And what does data separation look like on dedicated vs private?

If you can send a short cost comparison today I’ll share with our procurement lead and we can then pick a time for Marissa’s demo.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of ML Engineering, Acme Retail
elaine@acme.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & pricing follow-up

Thanks Elaine — good detail, that helps a lot. Below is a concise cost comparison and notes on burst/fallover options. I kept the math intentionally high-level; we can put exact numbers in the attached spreadsheet and adjust after you confirm token volumes.

Scenario assumptions (based on your numbers):
- 10M requests/month; avg 100 tokens/request => 1B tokens/month. Peak 600 QPS sustained for short windows.

Option A — Hosted API (pay-as-you-go):
- Unit pricing example: $0.0004 per token (generation + input).
- Monthly cost estimate: 1,000,000,000 tokens * $0.0004 = $400,000/month.
- Pros: no infra commitment, fastest onboarding, built-in autoscaling. Cons: higher unit cost at volume and less control over environment.

Option B — Dedicated capacity (reserved commit):
- Recommendation: start with a 2-GPU reserved pool optimized for inference (equivalent to 2x A100-class capacity) to meet baseline throughput and provide headroom for concurrent sessions.
- Example committed price: $20,000/month for the 2-GPU pool (note: exact SKU/pricing depends on region & VM footprint).
- Effective per-token equivalent (rough): if you amortize the committed cost over 1B tokens => ~$0.00002/token (significantly lower than hosted).
- Burst handling: yes — policy-based routing can route overflow to Redwood Hosted API at typical per-token rates. We can set a budget cap for hosted bursts.
- Data separation: Dedicated pools provide tenant isolation and optional network peering; logs/metrics can be routed to your VPC. For strict compliance, Private VPC/on-prem is recommended.

Option C — Private (VPC / on-prem):
- Similar to Dedicated from a performance standpoint but with customer-controlled networking and KMS/HSM. Typical pricing = dedicated capacity + private deployment fee & support (one-time onboarding + higher annual support).

Key tradeoffs:
- If you expect sustained >500M tokens/month long-term, Dedicated is almost always more economical.
- If you need strict EU residency + KMS control for certain data sets, recommend a hybrid: Dedicated in-region for regulated traffic + Hosted for global non-sensitive requests.

Next actions I propose:
1) Marissa to run a short throughput sizing demo (20-30 minutes) showing 600 QPS spikes and batch throughput.
2) We’ll update the attached pricing sheet with exact per-SKU committed prices and a second column showing effective per-request cost across monthly volumes.
3) Procurement intro if numbers look reasonable.

Are you available tomorrow 10–11am PT for the demo? If not, propose a slot and we’ll lock it in.

Cheers,
Aditya

Attachment: Acme_MA_Pricing_Model.xlsx
